name: Cerebras Systems
monetization: Sells wafer-scale AI systems and, increasingly, high-speed inference as a service (tokens/sec as the product); the main non-GPU architecture with real revenue.
description_md: Cerebras designs the Wafer-Scale Engine — a single dinner-plate-sized chip that replaces racks of GPUs — and sells both systems and Cerebras-hosted inference, where it claims the fastest token throughput available. After years as a G42-dependent private company (its 2024 S-1 showed the UAE group at ~87% of H1 2024 revenue), it landed a >$20B, 750MW multi-year inference deal with OpenAI in January 2026 and went public on May 14, 2026 in the year's breakout IPO: priced at $185 ($5.55B raised), it opened at $385 and ended day one around a ~$66B market cap.
ai_monetization_md: Two revenue lines: hardware/systems sales (CS-3 clusters to sovereigns and enterprises — G42/MBZUAI historically its two largest customers) and inference services sold per-token/per-capacity, now anchored by the OpenAI agreement to deploy 750MW of Cerebras compute (reported at >$20B over multiple years). 2025 revenue was $510M — meaning the OpenAI commitment alone is ~40× trailing revenue, committed rather than realized.
ai_strategy_md: Compete on inference speed rather than training-ecosystem breadth: wafer-scale SRAM bandwidth yields order-of-magnitude faster tokens on frontier models, which Cerebras sells to latency-sensitive buyers (agents, code, voice) — a wedge into Nvidia's inference share without fighting CUDA head-on for training. Diversification is the strategic through-line: from G42 concentration (which delayed its 2024 IPO amid CFIUS review of G42's stake) toward OpenAI, US hyperscale, and sovereign deals; the IPO proceeds fund US manufacturing and data-center capacity for the 750MW ramp.
risk_notes_md: Customer concentration is the recurring pattern, not an anecdote: G42 was ~83–87% of revenue in 2023–24, and the forward book now leans heavily on a single OpenAI contract — a counterparty that is itself loss-making with ~$600B+ of compute commitments (see `openai`). Execution risk on scaling wafer-scale manufacturing (TSMC-dependent) to 750MW; competitive response from Nvidia inference silicon and Groq-class rivals; day-one IPO pop means the public mark embeds high expectations (~$66B vs $510M 2025 revenue, ~130×).

events.why_it_matters: Transforms Cerebras's book from G42-dependent to OpenAI-anchored and validates non-Nvidia silicon at frontier-inference scale — while re-creating single-customer concentration one node over.
